basis: Insulin resistance; cardiomyopathy and cholestasis 3/3; lipoatrophy/hyperkeratosis 80-99%. Neurologic and muscle findings (30-79%) and renal findings omitted by cap.

decisions.neurologic: none: developmental disability occurs in 30-79%, but more frequent cardiac, hepatic and cutaneous disease exhaust the four-organ cap.
decisions.dermatologic: involved: subcutaneous fat loss and hyperkeratosis occur in 80-99%, establishing persistent cutaneous involvement.

basis: Autonomous adrenal aldosterone excess defines the endocrine disorder; sustained secondary hypertension occurs in over 90% and is a defining clinical manifestation.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: sustained hypertension is a defining manifestation in over 90%; hypertension explicitly belongs to the cardiovascular axis.

basis: Brittle sulfur-poor hair and severe neurodevelopmental disease 2/2; infections 2/2 with IgG1 deficiency 1/2; panhypopituitarism 1/2. Retinal/optic defects 1/2 omitted by cap.

decisions.neurologic: primary: profound intellectual disability, cerebellar abnormalities and progressive microcephaly in 2/2 establish a core neurodevelopmental phenotype.
decisions.ocular: none: retinal dystrophy and optic nerve hypoplasia occur in 1/2, but are excluded by the four-organ cap.
decisions.infectious_immune: primary: recurrent infections in 2/2 with documented chronic IgG1 deficiency in 1/2 support syndromic immunodeficiency, requiring the mechanism axis.

basis: Disseminated histiocytic neoplasm with defining marrow/splenic, skin and hepatic infiltration; destructive bone lesions are common (~50% or more). Other sites excluded by cap.

decisions.hepatic: primary: hepatic infiltration with hepatomegaly and possible jaundice is explicitly part of this disseminated disease's definition.
decisions.dermatologic: primary: infiltrative skin lesions are a defining presentation of Letterer-Siwe disease, rather than a transient rash.

basis: Developmental impairment and characteristic skeletal/digital malformations commonly define major chromosome 9 partial-gain syndromes; cardiac and renal abnormalities vary by segment.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: characteristic hand, phalangeal and other skeletal malformations are core features across the major partial chromosome 9 duplication phenotypes.

basis: Abnormal dentin and tooth-root development define disease; supplied HPO records structural bony exostoses in 30-79%. Increased bone density alone would not establish damage.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: HPO explicitly reports exostoses in 30-79%; these are structural bony lesions, beyond an isolated bone-density measurement.

basis: Developmental delay 5/5 and intellectual disability 4/4 establish the neurodevelopmental phenotype. Single-patient ocular observations do not establish common involvement.

decisions.ocular: none: cataract and retinopathy each have only a 1/1 assessed observation; prevalence of at least 30% across this syndrome is not established.

basis: Premature skin/subcutaneous aging and skeletal abnormalities characterize most major progeroid syndromes; vascular, endocrine, ocular and neurologic damage vary by subtype.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: skeletal hypoplasia, osteolysis, osteoporosis or contractures are core features across most major progeroid forms, although the particular lesions differ.

basis: Syndromic BBS predominates: retinal dystrophy, obesity and cognitive impairment (~50-60%) are major criteria; intrinsic renal disease ~30-50%. Polydactyly omitted by cap; isolated RP is rare.

decisions.renal: involved: intrinsic renal abnormalities or dysfunction affect approximately 30-50% of the predominant syndromic phenotype.
decisions.neurologic: primary: neurodevelopmental/cognitive impairment (~50-60%) is a major BBS diagnostic feature; rare isolated retinopathy does not determine this umbrella's labels.
decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: obesity (~70-90%) is a major diagnostic feature of the predominant Bardet-Biedl phenotype; isolated BBS2 retinopathy is a minority presentation.

basis: Capillary and arteriovenous malformations define vascular disease. Cutaneous discoloration does not establish skin injury; vein of Galen malformation occurs in only 1-4%.

decisions.dermatologic: none: the cutaneous marks reflect malformed dermal vessels; discoloration alone does not establish direct damage to skin tissue.
